Subject: Request for pen test exec summary and sharing options

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — the performance numbers looked promising. Our GRC team is asking for the latest penetration test executive summary and, if possible, a path to review the full report under NDA.

A few constraints from our side:
- We cannot accept redactions that remove asset identifiers used by our ops team (they need to verify remediation).
- We prefer watermarked PDFs or a secure viewer rather than emailed attachments.
- Procurement would like confirmation on turnaround (we have a compliance review window that closes 9/10).

Can you confirm how Redwood typically handles: secure viewers, watermarking, limited extracts, and whether you offer an escrowed encrypted archive for legal review? Also please flag any timelines for internal legal review on your side.

Appreciate it — we can hop on a quick call if that helps.

John

Director, Information Security
Acme Corp
john.doe@acme-corp.com

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for pen test exec summary and sharing options

Hi John — thanks for the clear context. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate the workflow you described. Below is our proposed path and timeline.

What we can offer
- Executive summary: deliverable via our secure viewer (no direct PDF sent). The viewer supports dynamic per-user watermarking (name, email, timestamp) and prevents printing/download by default.
- Full report review: available either as (A) time-limited secure viewer session with redaction overlays applied, or (B) an encrypted archive placed with a neutral escrow provider for in-person/legal review.
- Redaction approach: we provide a redaction matrix that lists vulnerability IDs, suggested redaction category (PII, third-party credentials, customer-specific artifacts), and the justification for each redaction. You can review the matrix and request adjustments.

Proposed timeline
- Today (09/01): I can send our standard NDA via DocuSign and a redaction_matrix_template.xlsx for your team to populate.
- After NDA signed: Redwood legal and security will turn the viewer access / redaction proposal around within 3 business days. If you prefer escrowed handback, that takes up to 5 business days due to packaging and encryption ops.

Attachments I will include:
- Redwood_NDA_Docusign.pdf (DocuSign link included below)
- redaction_matrix_template.xlsx (we use this to agree redaction boundaries)
- viewer_access_instructions.txt (how the secure viewer session works)

Notes/constraints
- We cannot share non-redacted raw exploit artifacts over email for liability reasons; these can be reviewed in the escrow or in-person under contract.
- If you need asset-level identifiers unredacted for verification, please annotate them in the redaction matrix; we can make targeted exceptions for named contacts with RBAC in the viewer.

If this approach works, please sign the NDA link I include below and drop the populated redaction matrix back to me. Happy to schedule a 20-min sync to walk through the viewer.

DocuSign link: https://docuSign.example/signer/ACME-NDA-12345
Viewer invite (post-NDA): https://secureviewer.redwood.example/invite/pt-execsum-acme

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for pen test exec summary and sharing options

Marcus / Sofia — legal has reviewed the ask. We can proceed with the secure viewer + DocuSign NDA path as the default. A few legal points to include in the DocuSign (I will add these clauses):
- Explicit carve-out for customer-owned asset identifiers when Acme marks them on the redaction matrix (so we avoid breaking verification).
- A clause allowing time-limited access under RBAC for up to 5 named reviewers (we'll request their names/emails).
- Chain-of-custody statement for any escrowed archive (manifest + signed hash).
- Standard indemnity/usage limitations remain; do not change those unless negotiated via sales/legal.

Watermarking: we will represent it contractually as a "forensic watermark" (visual + embedded metadata) and require that viewers attest in the NDA that they will not attempt to remove or alter watermarks. We should avoid promising irreversible cryptographic immutability unless our viewer generates signed, server-held audit logs — we do have audit logs and can provide slices on request.

Timing: legal can turn the NDA + redaction clause updates in 1 business day. Security will prepare the viewer packaging in parallel (3 business days post-NDA). For escrow packaging, ops will need 2–3 additional business days.

 Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
